## Final Accepted Amendments

### `fr-1-19ba7088`

**Classification:** fix_current_bead

docs/secret_sharing.md:127 documents a decrypted VSS share JSON shape that no longer matches the implementation: docs/secret_sharing.md:133-134 call the share and verifier fields base64 even though the code serializes hex strings, and docs/secret_sharing.md:136-144 still show a tagged `original_wallet` with `wallet_type`, `seed_phrase`, `descriptors`, and `public_keys`. The current schema stores `original_wallet` directly as `SinglesigPublicMetadataV0` (frozenkrill-core/src/wallet_description.rs:1347) and includes `blinder_share_data` plus optional `*_hi` fields (frozenkrill-core/src/wallet_description.rs:1331). Update the docs example and file-format text so users and future maintainers do not rely on the removed enum/tagged layout or expect fields that are not present.

### `fr-1-4a3963db`

**Classification:** propose_new_bead

Refresh the share-file JSON example in docs/secret_sharing.md:127-146. The current example is doubly inaccurate: (a) the `wallet_type: "singlesig"` discriminator line was just invalidated by this bead's enum drop — `original_wallet` is now a flat `SinglesigPublicMetadataV0` with no tag — and (b) the example was already drifting before x2z, showing fictional fields (`seed_phrase`, `descriptors`, `public_keys`) that do not exist anywhere in the real `SinglesigPublicMetadataV0` struct (which actually has `singlesig_xpub`, `master_fingerprint`, `singlesig_derivation_path`, `multisig_xpub`, `multisig_derivation_path`, `singlesig_first_address`, `singlesig_receiving_output_descriptor`, `singlesig_change_output_descriptor`, `is_duress`, etc.). The example should be regenerated against the actual serialized JSON of a real VSS share so it reflects what users will actually see when inspecting a decrypted share. Also note `blinder_share_data`, `share_data_hi`, `blinder_share_data_hi`, and `verification_data_hi` fields are missing from the example. Recommend replacing with a serde_json output captured from one of the round-trip tests (e.g. test_random_24_word_round_trip) so it is generated rather than hand-maintained.
